topic: Lambda Init Capture Emulation using std::bind (C++11)
explanation: Assumption: C++11 lambdas cannot capture move-only types by value. Reality: While direct value capture fails for move-only types, this limitation can be circumvented using `std::bind`. Why It Works: The object is moved into the `std::bind` object itself during the creation of the bind expression. The resulting `std::bind` object (which acts like the closure) then passes the internal copy/reference of that object to the actual C++11 lambda body as an argument. This technique is verbose but necessary for moving resources like `std::unique_ptr` into asynchronous contexts prior to C++14.
practical_example: Maintaining a legacy C++11 codebase that requires passing a `std::thread` object into a callable object that outlives the current scope. Since `std::thread` is move-only, `std::bind` must be used as an intermediary to facilitate the transfer of ownership.
chapter: Item 32: Use init capture to move objects into closures
book: Effective Modern C++ by Scott Meyers
